ONE_TINY_FIGURE — exactly one human-scale figure rendered TINY (occupying ~2% of the frame), placed mid-distance for scale. The figure is back-turned or in profile, never in close detail. Pose conveys the story beat through silhouette.
ONE_SHIP_SMALL — exactly one sci-fi craft rendered SMALL (occupying ~5% of the frame), crossing or hovering at mid-distance. The ship is detailed but the environment dominates.

FIGURE_PLUS_SHIP — one tiny figure on terrain + one small ship in air or descending. Two scale anchors at different elevations. The composition implies the figure arrived via the ship, or the ship has come for the figure.
TINY_CARAVAN — a small procession of 3-5 figures or 3-5 ships moving across the frame. The collective is small in scale but visible. Conveys exodus, migration, formation.

FIGURES_AS_ANTS — multiple humanoid silhouettes rendered as tiny specks (each occupying <1% of frame) on a vast structure or terrain. The structure is the hero. The figures prove the scale is monumental.

TWO_FIGURES_MEETING — two figures positioned for a quiet exchange — one approaching, one waiting; or both facing the same horizon. Story beat is between them. Rendered small-to-medium in the environment.

LANDSCAPE_ONLY — no figures, no ships. Scale conveyed entirely through geological / architectural / atmospheric features. Reserved for scenes where the environment alone carries the story (impossible weather, dramatic light moment).

FOREGROUND_FIGURE_BACK — single figure in foreground, rendered medium-to-large but seen from BEHIND or in silhouette so face is not detailed. The figure watches the wonder unfold ahead of them. Classic Caspar-Friedrich / Spielberg awe-pose.
